title: Rygge Munitions Storage rea Expansion
description: The purpose of this amendment is to extend the deadline for submission of RFIs to 25 August 2026, extend the deadline for submission of proposals to 18 September 2026, provide an updated BLA template, and make various revisions to the solicitation in response to RFIs received. All amended language within the solicitation will be bolded and highlighted where possible for visibility........................................................................PROJECT TITLE: RYGGE MUNITIONS STORAGE AREA EXPANSIONPROJECT LOCATION: RYGGE, NORWAYTHIS CONSTRUCTION PROJECT WILL BE A COMPETITIVE, FIRM-FIXED PRICE DESIGN-BID-BUILD CONTRACT PROCURED VIA A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP) IN ACCORDANCE WITH FAR PARTS 15 AND 36 AND THE TRADEOFF SOURCE SELECTION PROCESS. THIS IS AN UNRESTRICTED (FULL-AND-OPEN COMPETITION) RFP WITH A BRAND-NAME REQUIREMENT UNDER NAICS CODE 236220. THE SMALL BUSINESS SIZE STANDARD FOR THIS NAICS CODE IS $45,000,000.00.The United States Corps of Engineers Europe District has a requirement on behalf of the United States Air Force (USAF) to build and extend the munitions storage area (MSA) on Rygge Air Station in support of USAF contingency operations in Norway. The project includes the construction of 20 ammunition storage magazines (earth-covered magazines, or ECMs) to accommodate a total Net Explosive Weight (NEW) of 3,000,000 pounds. A standard ammunition storage magazine design which supports up to a maximum capacity of 165,000 pounds NEW will be used for all 20 magazine/bunkers. Supporting facilities include three concrete munitions assembly pads (two 150 ft by 150 ft pads and one 250 ft by 250 ft pad), gravel roads, bermed areas, lighting, security fencing surmounted by barbed wire, and utility connections for communications and electrical. This project is in direct support of the European Deterrence Initiative (EDI) and the Supplementary Defense Cooperation Agreement (SDCA) between the United States and the Government of Norway, and is intended to be compatible with applicable NATO, DoD, Air Force, and host-nation design standards.

title: SOLE SOURCE: Prosensing Calibrations for the OMAO Aircraft Operations Center in Lakeland, FL.
description: The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration�s (NOAA) Acquisition and Grants Office, Eastern Acquisition Division-Kansas City intends to negotiate and award a purchase order, on a sole source basis, under authority of RFO FAR 6.103-1, with small business entity Prosensing, Inc. for specialized engineering, calibration, and data validation services for the Stepped Frequency Microwave Radiometer -High Altitude (SFMR-HA) system for the OMAO Aircraft Operations Center. Sole Source Justification: The sole source determination is based on NOAA�s Sole Source Justification. Only one source is capable of providing the supplies or services required at the level of quality required because the supplies or services ordered are unique or highly specialized. ProSensing Inc. is the sole source capable of performing hardware-level modifications and specialized temperature- dependent calibration for the SFMR-HA due to their proprietary hardware ownership and specialized testing facilities. No other vendor possesses the requisite equipment or proprietary technical data to deliver validated operational calibration constants within the required timelines. Operational readiness of the SFMR-HA on the high-altitude aircraft (G-IV/G-550) is critical to NOAA's hurricane surveillance and atmospheric sampling missions. Any delay in finalizing calibration constants will directly impede flight software accuracy during upcoming hurricane field operations. This pre-solicitation notice is not a request for competitive proposals and no solicitation package is available. However, firms that believe they can fully meet the government�s requirements may submit substantiating documentation or a request for additional information in writing to the (Contract Specialist) within 15 days after publication of this presolicitation notice. Such requests and documentation will be evaluated solely for the purpose of determining whether or not to conduct this procurement on a competitive basis. A determination by the government not to conduct a competitive procurement, based upon responses to this notice, is solely within the discretion of the government. Oral communications are not acceptable in response to this pre-solicitation notice.

title: Marine Atlantic Inc. – Port aux Basques Navigation Improvement Project
description: Marine Atlantic Inc. – Port aux Basques Navigation Improvement Project Notice of Request for Proposals Name of Procuring Entity:  Marine Atlantic Inc. (“MAI”) Contact Person:  Katie Clark, Director, Supply Chain Management ler2025@ma.ca Description of Procurement: Marine Atlantic Inc. is conducting a request for proposals (“RFP”) process for the removal of a landmass known as “Vardys Rock” and associated breakwater improvement (“Pikes I.”) both located in Port aux Basques Harbour in the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada.  (See Canadian Hydrographic Service Chart #4641, Port aux Basques and Approaches/et les Approches, for location reference only. Note: Vardys Rock referenced as Vardys I.)  The project’s objective is to improve navigational constraints impacting Marine Atlantic’s operations and vessel maneuvering restrictions, in addition to the development of new land to improve harbour protection and enhance lobster habitat.   Work in this project will include the following:  •    The demolition and disposal of all miscellaneous structures, debris, and electrical components on Vardys Rock; •    The relocation and disposal of overburden on Vardys Rock to an offsite location; •    The removal of remaining earth materials and bedrock of and surrounding Vardys Rock to an elevation of -9.5m Chart Datum (with material relocation to an infill area adjacent to the nearby Pikes I.. The infill area will be reinforced by armourstone on all faces.   Construction will involve established marine techniques including drilling, blasting, dredging and excavation with material reused where possible to maximize efficiency and reduce waste.   Construction is expected to take approximately one year exclusive of removal of temporary infrastructure.   The RFP process will involve negotiation and will not involve an electronic auction. Procurement Documents: Prospective suppliers who are interested in participating in the RFP process are required to execute and return a confidentiality agreement in order to obtain access to the RFP documents and the data site that MAI will use for the RFP process. Prospective suppliers should email ler2025@ma.ca to request a copy of the confidentiality agreement.   Construction  Period: Completion of construction will be required by the end of Q1 2028.  Permitted Jurisdictions and Applicable Trade Agreements: This RFP process is being conducted in accordance with the Government of Canada's Policy on Prioritizing Canadian Suppliers and Canadian Content in Strategic Federal Procurements and is therefore only open to Canadian Suppliers or Suppliers of an applicable trading partner as such terms are defined in such policy.  The government procurement agreements that apply to this procurement are the Canadian Free Trade Agreement, the Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement, the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership and the Canada-United Kingdom Trade Continuity Agreement.  Proponent Selection: MAI intends to conduct a prequalification as the first phase of the RFP and will prequalify up to three prequalified proponents who will participate in the second phase.  MAI intends to select a preferred proponent at the conclusion of the procurement process using a combined technical and financial score based on the following criteria. Organizational structure and project experience of Proponents providing similar services Proposed construction methodology inclusive of regulatory compliance, and effective measures so as to not impact harbour traffic and operations of Marine Atlantic Financial capacity; Pricing; The evaluation criteria are described in more detail in the RFP documents. Language of Submission:  Proposals are to be submitted in English. Address and Final Date for Submissions: Proposals must be submitted electronically on or before December 11, 2026 at 4:00 PM Atlantic Standard Time on the project data site.  The proposals will not be opened publicly. Single Proponent Structure: Proponent Team Members are only permitted to join a single Proponent.  This applies to all Proponent Team Members.  Notes: Prospective suppliers should note that information contained within this notice is subject to change. Prospective suppliers are encouraged to consult the RFP documents which contain the most current information.  If there is a conflict between the RFP documents and this notice, the RFP documents will take precedence.  Bidding and Documents are available on http://www.merx.com. Fees may apply; See https://www.merx.com/public/pricing for more information.

Muuttojen tilaaminen ei ole keskitettyä laajoissa tilaajaorganisaatioissa, joten yksittäisten muuttojen tilaajia voi olla useita tarpeesta riippuen. Hankinnalla tavoitellaankin yhteistyökumppania, joka on Tilaajien kokonaisvaltaisena tukena muuttojen valmistelussa sekä toteuttamisessa. Hankintaa ei ole jaettu osiin. Hankinnassa valitaan yksi (1) Toimittaja. Hankintaa ei jaeta osiin. Hankintayksiköt ovat arvioineet hankinnan jakamista osiin hankinnan valmistelun yhteydessä tehdyn markkinavuoropuhelun perusteella. Selvityksen perusteella hankinnan kohde muodostaa käyttötarkoituksensa, toimeksiantojen yhteensovittamisen sekä vastuunjaon näkökulmasta yhden toiminnallisen kokonaisuuden. Hankinnan toteuttaminen yhtenä kokonaisuutena mahdollistaa palvelutuotannon ja sopimusvastuiden selkeän hallinnan yhden kokonaisvastuullisen sopimuskumppanin kautta. Tämän vuoksi hankinnan toteuttaminen yhtenä kokonaisuutena on hankinnan luonne ja hankintayksikön tarpeet huomioon ottaen perusteltua. Tilaajien ostot vuodelta 2025 olivat: Vantaan ja Keravan hyvinvointialue: noin 60 000 € alv 0 % vuodessa Vantaan ja Keravan hyvinvointialue toimeentulotuki- ja vammaispalvelun asiakkaiden muutot: noin 60 000 € alv 0 % vuodessa Vantaan kaupunki ja sen tytäryhtiöt: noin 400 000 alv 0 % vuodessa TIlaajat ei sitoudu hankintamääriin. Vantaan ja Keravan hyvinvointialue julkaisee tämän tarjouspyynnön ja kilpailutuksen perusteella tehdään Vantaan kaupungille sekä Vantaan ja Keravan hyvinvointialueelle omat sopimukset kilpailutuksen voittaneen tarjoajan kanssa. Molemmat hankintayksiköt tekevät myös oman hankintapäätöksen. title: Luxembourg – Building installation work – CHL NBC VE VE 4744 OP-/ Untersuchungsleuchten
description: Das Klinikum Centre Hospitalier de Luxembourg beabsichtigt im Zuge des Neubaus mehrere deckenhängende OP-/ Untersuchungsleuchten (inkl. Transformatoren / Unterkonstruktionen / Schnittstellenplatten) gemäß dem Vergabeverfahren „Buch II Wettbewerblicher Dialog im Verhandlungsverfahren (Loi, Art. 63 und 67)" zu beschaffen. Bestandteil der Ausschreibung ist die Lieferung und Montage von: - 70 Untersuchungsleuchte LED (80 kLux) - 3 Untersuchungsleuchte, LED (80 kLux) mit einem Ausleger für Kontrastmittelinjektor - 1 Untersuchungsleuchte (LED 80 kLux) mit einem Ausleger inkl. Plattform (ca. 50 x 40 cm) - 7 Untersuchungsleuchte, LED (100 kLux) - 3 OP-Leuchte, LED (100 kLux), inkl. Vorhaltung Kamerasystem - 6 OP-Leuchte, LED (100 + 100 kLux), inkl. Vorhaltung Kamerasystem - 9 OP-Leuchte, LED (160 + 160 kLux), mit Kamerasystem - 7 OP-Leuchte, LED (160 + 160 kLux), mit Kamerasystem, unter LAF-Decke Inklusive der Schnittstelle (kompatible Steuerungsschnittstellen bzw. Software- /Hardwarekomponenten) zwischen den OP-Leuchten und dem bauseitigen Tableau (Touchscreen). Unterstützung zur Programmierung der Darstellung des Bedienfeldes im bauseitigen Tableau ist zu gewährleisten. Die Lieferung und Montage der Bestandteile soll nach dem folgenden Prioritäten-Schema getrennt ablaufen: Montage Unterkonstruktionen, Montage Leuchten, Lieferung Zubehör unmittelbar vor Inbetriebnahme (Diebstahlprävention). 1 Haupt- und 1 Nachbesserungstermin sind mit dem Angebotspreis abgegolten, wobei die Teilleistungen gemäß Terminplan gestaffelt einzutakten und mit der örtlichen Bauleitung/Fachbauleitung abzustimmen sind. Die gesetzliche Verjährungsfrist der Gewährleistungsansprüche beginnt mit der Abnahme der Leistung. Der Tag der Abnahme (komplette Montage inklusive Mängelbeseitigungen) ist der Gewährleistungsbeginn. Folgende Leistungen sind neben den gerätebezogenen Leistungen anzubieten und zu kalkulieren: - Bei der Kollisionsprüfung durch den koordinierenden Architekten (4Bund) ist durch den Auftragnehmer (AN) mitzuwirken. Die Montagepläne sind bei Erfordernis anzupassen. - Für Organisationsbesprechungen - auch teil- und abschnittsweise - hat der AN einen mit der Anlage in allen Teilen technisch und betrieblich vertrauten, sachkundigen Mitarbeiter beizustellen. - Weitere Leistungen gemäß den zusätzlichen technischen Vorbemerkungen der Medizintechnik. Für die Lieferungen und Montagen der Geräte sind folgende Termine maßgebend: Möglicher Beginn Einbau: 08.09.2027 Spätester Abschluss Montagen: 29.03.2029 (Innenausbau + Technik gem. Generalablaufplan_V5) Unter Berücksichtigung des Starttermins ist ein Montageterminplan vorzulegen und ggf. an Vorgaben des Architekten (4Bund) anzupassen. Die jeweils für die Einbringung und Montage benötigten Zeiten sind pro Gerät zu hinterlegen.

title: MP Police Outfitting - Repair and Overhaul (R&O)
description: File Number: W8486-270799/A MP Police Outfitting - Repair and Overhaul (R&O) Amendment 002. This amendment is raised to extend the closing date from September 2, 2026, to September 18, 2026. (Amendment 002 PDF has been attached) --------------------------------------------------------------- Question 1. The document calls for the Whelen Cenator Lightbar which is what is currently being used; however, the lightbar has been discontinued by Whelen and replaced by the Edge 9X lightbar. Will this be an acceptable alternative? Answer: If the Whelen Edge 9X is compatible with the equipment currently installed in our patrol vehicles and provides the same functionality as the Whelen Cenator, I have no objection to its use as a replacement. Question 2. The document mentions the Setina Vault Lock at one point, the Setina Blac-Rac at another, and then lists the part number for the Setina gun rack that was custom made for the Federal Government (RCMP, DND, etc.) All three are different models. Is the rack currently being installed into the units acceptable? Answer: The only weapon rack approved and accepted by the Federal Government is the SET-GK07222UXLRCMP (the Setina gun rack custom-manufactured for Federal Government agencies such as the RCMP, DND, and Military Police). Question 3. The document mentions the "MDT tray repeater" to be supplied by DND however Adj. Simard-Desroches mentioned that this would be installed by the bases upon receiving the completed units. Is this being added back into the upfits? Answer: The CF-33 MDT docking station will be installed by the supplier. The MDT tray repeater will be installed separately by DND. Question 4. For the requirement below is DND looking for an installation facility in each province or one for Western Canada i.e.: Albert, Central Canada i.e.: Ontario, Eastern Canada i.e.: Nova Scotia? 4.1.6 The repair and overhaul contract must have regionalized facilities to provide the above services in the following areas: Western Canada – BC to Manitoba; Central Canada – Ontario and Quebec; and Eastern Canada – New Brunswick to Newfoundland. Answer: Yes. From a logistics perspective, having a facility in each province would be preferable. This would facilitate the movement of new patrol vehicles and significantly reduce delivery timelines. Question 5. Will DND consider having all the vehicle delivered to one location in Ontario using the vehicle manufacture ship through process for up fitting? Upon completion the vehicles would than be shipped to final location? Answer: No. The manufacturer delivers the vehicles to the government-designated dealership in each province (close to the Base). The MAJ EQP or local fleet managers then pick up the vehicles from the dealerships. An EMO is subsequently created to assign a CFR to the vehicle. Once this process is complete, the patrol vehicles are delivered to the supplier for upfitting. Question 6. Police Lights General: RECOMMENDED POLICE LIGHT PARTS Whelen products are strongly recommended due to reliability, replacement low cost, continuity and parts availability in Canada. Will DND accept Canadian manufacture equivalent lights and light bar by D & R Electronics. Manufactured in Canada with lower cost, higher continuity and parts availability than US manufactured lights. Answer: It is the supplier's responsibility to provide sufficient documentation demonstrating that the proposed alternative meets the required specifications. As outlined in the SOW: "Substitutes and alternatives that are equivalent in product, performance or standard will be considered accepted by the Technical Authority when proof of conformance of equivalence for the respective requirement is provided for evaluation." Question 7. The question is also what is to be entered in these tables. The other tables covered the pricing in the three regions. Are these tables the collective total price of the three regions? Answer: Yes this is the total price of the 3 regions ---------- Amendment 001 This amendment is raised to correct the wording in the Annex Evaluated Aggregate Price of the Bid on Table 1 and Table 2 (Amendment 001 PDF has been attached) ---------- File Number: W8486-270799/A MP Police Outfitting - Repair and Overhaul (R&O) PROPOSED PROCUREMENT The Department of National Defence (DND) has a requirement for the Repair and Overhaul (R&O of modification, testing, calibration, and reduction to spares of the Military Police (MP) vehicles for Outfitting. This requirement includes the services of a licensed contractor to install policing equipment on new MP vehicles. The removal of equipment is referring to decommissioning vehicles to have items removed from old vehicles such as emergency equipment, safety equipment, communications equipment and police markings, on Military Police (MP) vehicles. Additionally, the repair and overhaul contract requires repair and maintenance services on the new equipment installed into the new vehicle. The contractor will be responsible for providing qualified on-site labour, specified materials, a secure compound or facility for the storage of vehicles awaiting work and/or shipment, and supervision of the process. The work will be carried out for a period of three (3) years from the effective date of contract award with an option to extend the contract for one (1) additional periods of one (1) year. The crown retains the rights to negotiate with suppliers on any procurement. Documents may be submitted in either official language of Canada. Submission of Bids This requirement uses electronic receipts of bids by e-mail only. For details, please review the section entitled Electronic Submission of Bids in the solicitation document. Bids must be submitted by e-mail only to the following e-mail address: DLP53BidsReceiving.DAAT53Receptiondessoumissions@forces.gc.ca Debriefings Bidders may request a debriefing on the results of the bid solicitation process. Bidders should make the request to the Contracting Authority within fifteen (15) working days from receipt of the results of the bid solicitation process. title: Switzerland – Architectural and related services – Ausbildungszentrum Riedikon, Neubau Logistik- und Verwaltungszentrum
description: Auf dem Grundstück Kat.-Nr. L1340, Bühlenweg 20 in Riedikon, betreibt die Leistungsgruppe Bevölkerungsschutz der Stadt Uster ein Ausbildungszentrum. Die Grundstücksfläche umfasst total 28'573 m2, wovon für das Ausbildungszentrum 10'400 m2, für die Vermietung an den Hundeclub 4600 m2 und für die landwirtschaftliche Verpachtung 9300 m2 genutzt werden. 4273 m2 sind Restfläche mit Wald und Moor. Das Ausbildungszentrum besteht aus diversen Übungsgebäuden und -flächen, sowie den zugehörigen Garderoben-, Schulungs-, Verwaltungs- und Lagerräumen. Die beiden Brandhäuser wurden in den vergangenen Jahren neu erstellt und sind auf dem neuesten Stand. Die Nebengebäude sind teilweise in einem schlechten Zustand und dringend sanierungsbedürftig. Mit dem Unterpachtvertrag für das Areal Zeughaus West an eine gemeinnützige Wohnbaugenossenschaft muss der Zivilschutz in absehbarer Zeit dieses Areal verlassen und benötigt neue Einstellflächen für die Fahrzeuge und einen Ort für den Zusammenzug. Aus diesen beiden Gründen wurde entschieden, das Ausbildungszentrum um ein neues Logistik- und Verwaltungszentrum zu erweitern. So kann der gesamte Zivilschutz an einem zentralen Ort untergebracht und Schulungen abgehalten werden.

title: MARSOC Advance Training Company (ATC)
description: Action: Notice of Intent to Sole Source Agency: U.S. Special Operations Command (USSOCOM) Contracting Office: Marine Corps Forces Special Operations Command (MARSOC) Classification Code: NAICS: 541611 � Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services PSC: R499 - SUPPORT- PROFESSIONAL: OTHER Subject: Intent to Award a Sole Source Contract for Marine Raider Training Center (MRTC) Advance Training Company (ATC) Full Time Equivalent (FTE). 1. Description of Requirement: The U.S. Marine Corps Forces Special Operations Command (MARSOC) intends to award a single-award Definitive Contract to Threat Tec LLC to provide precise and effective special reconnaissance operations that are fully coordinated and synchronized among all components of USSOCOM and key interagency organizations. The ATC program requires contracted support for exercise design, development, and management, scenario constructions, and tailored training support. The contractor shall provide formal training to individual Critical Skills Operators (CSO) in Advanced SR skills to provide qualified CSO�s to the Marine Special Operations Companies (MSOCs). The unit specifically charged with this responsibility is the MRTC. Due to the small size of the MRTC staff, contractor assistance is required to support the Special Reconnaissance, Instructor Sustainment Courses, and other Advanced SR Courses. The resultant contract will have a one-year basis for a total estimated price of $2,994,950.40. 2. Authority: This action is being conducted on a sole-source basis under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), as implemented by FAR Overhaul 6.103-1 for the acquisition of noncommercial services using Negotiated Contracting Procedures under RFO Part 15. 3. Rationale for Sole Source: Threat Tec, LLC is the incumbent contractor currently executing the MRTC ATC course curriculum, exercise design, full-mission profiles, and scenario development. An immediate bridge is required to prevent catastrophic lapses in specialized training pipelines for Marines Special Operations Companies (MSOCs) and Critical Skills Operators (CSOs) deploying to global operational areas. This bridge contract is essential to prevent a critical gap in mission-essential training services while USSOCOM finalizes, awards, and fully implements its comprehensive, enterprise-wide SOF Global Services Delivery (SOFGSD) contract in the fiscal year of 2027. SOFGSD will replace the prior SOF Core Support Services contract. The contract covers the full range of knowledge-based services supporting U.S.-based and globally assigned Special Operations Forces, from training and program management to intelligence support engineering and administrative services. Awarding an alternate contractor for this interim bridge period would introduce substantial, mission-degrading delays. The advanced ATC curriculum requires cleared, highly vetted personnel with existing institutional knowledge of MARFORSOC and USSOCOM Tactics, Techniques, and Procedures (TTPs). Any phase-in/ramp-up period would compromise active, scheduled course iterations. Transitioning to a new vendor for an interim period prior to onboarding onto the SOFGSD vehicle would result in significant duplicate mobilization and phase-in costs that cannot be recovered through competition. 4. Notice to Industry: All responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation within fifteen (15) calendar days of publication of this notice, which shall be considered by the Government. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Capability statements received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement in lieu of this sole-source action. 5. Submission Instructions: All capability statements must be submitted via email to the Contracting Officer, Jordan D. Orellana Buitron, at jordan.d.orellanabuitron.mil@socom.mil and Contracting Specialist, Ger Yang, at ger.yang.mil@socom.mil.

Netherlands – Firefighting, rescue and safety equipment – Warmtebeeldcamera's t.b.v. Brandweer Twente
description: De VRT wenst per perceel één Opdrachtnemer te contracteren voor de levering van warmtebeeldcamera’s (WBC’s) en bijbehorende toebehoren. De WBC’s worden ingezet ter ondersteuning van brandbestrijding, technische hulpverlening en incidentbestrijding en dragen bij aan de veiligheid en effectiviteit van hulpverleners tijdens operationele inzet. De aanbesteding omvat de volgende percelen: • Perceel 1 – Decision Making Camera: warmtebeeldcamera voor gebruik onder zware en extreme omstandigheden, met nadruk op hittebestendigheid, robuustheid en besluitvorming tijdens inzet. • Perceel 2 – Situational Awareness Camera: persoonlijke warmtebeeldcamera voor oriëntatie in rook, detectie van thermische sporen en ondersteuning van de individuele veiligheid, met minimale bediening en een gewicht van maximaal 500 gram. Onder WBC’s en toebehoren worden verstaan: accessoires, laders, accu’s, software, onderhouds- en reparatiemogelijkheden, technische ondersteuning, updates en training. Raamovereenkomst; geen gegarandeerde afname.

description: 1. Summary Environment and Climate Change Canada has a requirement for on demand technical support and expertise for the continuous improvement of two established CGE models used to assess climate policy impacts. The two models are EC-PRO and EC-MSMR as detailed in the Statement of Work, Annex A to the bid solicitation. The period of the Contract is for three years from date of Contract Award. 2. Reciprocal Procurement - Limited Supplier Eligibility Solicitation of Offer Submission Eligibility. This solicitation of offers is subject to the Policy on Reciprocal Procurement. This means that only Canadian Suppliers and Suppliers of an Applicable Trading Partner, as defined in the Attachment 1 to Part 1 Solicitation of Offers Definitions, are eligible for this solicitation of offers. Offers submitted by Suppliers of a Non-Trading Partner will be rejected. 5. Service Requirements For services requirements, bidders in receipt of a pension or a lump sum payment must provide the required information as detailed in article 3 of Part 2 of the bid solicitation. 6. Trade Agreements The requirement is subject to the provisions of the of the Canadian Free Trade Agreement (CFTA), the Canada–Chile Free Trade Agreement, the Canada–Colombia Free Trade Agreement, the Canada–Honduras Free Trade Agreement, the Canada–Korea Free Trade Agreement, the Canada–Panama Free Trade Agreement, Canada-Peru Free Trade Agreement, the Comprehensive Economic Free Trade Agreement [CETA], the World Trade Organization – Agreement on Government Procurement [WTO-AGP], the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership [CPTPP] and the Canada-Ukraine Free Trade Agreement. 7. Social Procurement Environment and Climate Change Canada supports the Government of Canada’s social and economic objectives, including increasing the participation of businesses from under-represented groups in government procurement opportunities. As such, bidders owned or led by Canadians from under-represented groups, such as women, LGBTQ2+ persons, persons with disabilities and persons from visible minorities are encouraged to submit a bid to this opportunity. 8. Debriefings Bidders may request a debriefing on the results of the bid solicitation process. Bidders should make the request to the Contracting Authority within 15 working days from receipt of the results of the bid solicitation process. The debriefing may be in writing, by telephone or in person. 9. Official Languages Environment and Climate Change Canada provides procurement services in both official languages. Bidders may submit a bid in the official language of their choice. 10. Additional Information For additional information, interested suppliers must contact the Contracting Officer named in this Notice.

title: Joe Pool Dam Slide Repairs
description: PRESOLICITATION NOTICE ONLY - Proposed Solicitation Number - W9126G26BA010 posted on or about 18 September 2026. Contract for Joe Pool Dam Slide Repair at Joe Pool Lake, Texas. This announcement is a competitive small business set aside, firm-fixed price, Joe Pool Dam Slide Repair civil works construction services at Joe Pool Lake, Texas. The North American Industry Classification System code (NAICS) for this procurement is 237990-Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction which has a small business size standard of $45 Million. The Product Service Code is Z2PC-Repair or Alteration of Dams. The solicitation is anticipated to be issued on or about 14 September 2026, and proposals due on or about 15 October 2026. Project Scope: The contractor shall repair four shallow slides (Slides 18, 20, 21, and 28) on the upstream and downstream dam embankment slopes. Work includes the removal of slide debris; excavation of the slide area with bench-cutting into the stable embankment and a keyway into the foundation toe; lime-treatment of excavated soil; placement and compaction of treated soil to restore original design contours; and final surface restoration with riprap on the upstream slope and topsoil with vegetation on the downstream slope.

title: C1DA--Engineering Services IDIQ - Erie VA
description: Engineering Services Firms for a Single Award Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Design Contract This announcement is for the selection of a single Engineering Services (ES) Firm for an Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Design contract for the Department of Veterans Affairs, Erie VA Medical Center located in Erie, Pennsylvania. Projects will be for the Erie VA Medical Center. Work will be required on an as needed basis and will be awarded by use of Firm Fixed Price Task Orders. The Government intends to award a Firm Fixed Price Contract. All potential offerors must provide a SF 330 containing all required information listed below. The form format must be the General Services Administration SF 330 found on the GSA Forms Library website. The resultant award shall be established as a single five (5) year contract. Total value of the contract shall not exceed $7,000,000.00 CONTRACT INFORMATION: The Engineering Services IDIQ contract may be used for a wide range of design services. Primarily the Task Orders will be used, but not limited to, design of new commercial/industrial type facilities and to design renovations of existing facilities. All contract awards will incorporate the attached Scope of Work dated June 16, 2026, attached. Expected ES services may require any combination of the following: Title I Site Investigation Services, Title I - Design Services, and Title II Construction Period Services. This contract is being procured in accordance with the Brooks AE Act as implemented in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Subpart 36.6, Veterans Administration Acquisition Regulation (VAAR) 836.6 and Veterans Affairs Acquisition Manual (VAAM) M836.6. Firms will be selected for presentations based on demonstrated competence and qualifications for required work. This contract is set-aside 100% for Service Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business s (SDVOSB) capable of completing work under the North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code 541330. A Firm Fixed Price (FFP) contract will be awarded with a minimum $2,000.00 guarantee. The minimum guarantee for the entire contract term will be satisfied by the award of the initial Task Order. SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS: Interested firms having the capabilities to perform this work must submit an email copy of the Standard Form 330 (SF 330) Parts I and II. Please note this is not a request for proposal. Eligible responses received will be evaluated and the top three (3) most highly qualified firms will be compiled on a shortlist of candidates who will be contacted for an interview. For the evaluation, Professional Qualifications to Perform the Services Required, Specialized Experience and Technical Competence, are significantly more important than the other five (5) factors and are of equal weight. The remaining five (5) factors are of equal weight among themselves. The following evaluation criteria shall be used to evaluate firms and determine the most highly qualified firm for possible contract award. A. Professional Qualifications necessary for satisfactory performance: This is intended to evaluate the personnel and their related qualifications. The key positions should include Project Managers, Quality Assurance Manager, Architects, Structural Engineers, Electrical Engineers, Mechanical Engineers, Fire Protection Engineers, and Interior Designers. Firm should indicate whether these personnel have professional certifications in particular field, i.e. PE in Mechanical Engineering. The evaluation board shall consider the specific experience and qualifications (i.e., education, training, registration, certifications, overall relevant experience, and longevity with the firm) of personnel proposed for assignment to the project, and their record of working together as a team when evaluating professional qualifications. The lead designer in each discipline must be registered but does not have to be registered in the particular state where the project is located. B. Specialized Experience and Technical Competence: This factor evaluates the experience of the firm and design team in completing projects requiring skills similar to those anticipated for this contract. This may include general renovation of medical center space to include architectural changes of walls, ceilings, floors, finishes, carpentry, masonry, doorways including hardware, electrical, plumbing including storm sewer, sanitary, hot and cold water, Heating, ventilating, Air conditioning (HVAC) to include, package units, variable air and constant air volume terminals with reheat, Variable frequency drive air handlers, steam and condensate piping, primary and secondary electrical circuits, digital controls, fire protection to include sprinkle system, central fire and security alarms, audio paging systems, asbestos abatement and all work to return space to finished, functioning condition. Experience providing drawings in 3D. Designing general construction of new space to include structural work, roofing, exterior walls, site work, site utilities and work as stated above. Design of specialty construction may include tuck pointing, asphalt paving, elevators, complete key system, large centrifugal chillers and Boiler controls. Extra consideration may be given for experience designing projects for Department of Veterans Affairs Facilities. The evaluation board shall consider at least five (5) similar projects and how well the proposal addresses technical capabilities in design quality management procedures, CAD Building Information Modeling, equipment resources, and laboratory requirements for the firm and any proposed subcontractors. Where appropriate, the evaluation board will also evaluate their experience in energy conservation, pollution prevention, waste reduction and the use of recovered materials. The effectiveness of their proposed project team (including management structure, coordination of disciplines, subcontractors, and prior working relationships) should also be examined. NOTE: Ensure that projects listed were completed by the firm as the prime contractor and not as a subcontractor or projects completed by key personnel while employed by another firm C. Past Performance: Past performance on contracts with Government agencies (Particularly Department of Veterans Affairs) and private industry in terms of cost control, quality of work and compliance with performance schedules. When evaluating past performance, the evaluation board shall consider superior performance ratings on recently completed VA projects as well as the reputation and standing of the firm and its principal officials with respect to professional performance, general management, and cooperativeness. Also, consider, as appropriate, the record of significant claims against the firm because of improper or incomplete architectural and engineering services. D. Capacity to accomplish the work in the required time: This factor evaluates the ability of the Engineering Services firm to, given their current projected workload and the availability of their key personnel, to accomplish the project in the required time. When evaluating capacity, the evaluation board shall consider the volume of work awarded by VA during the previous 12 months. Use data extracted from the Federal Procurement Data System. Consider the full potential value of any current indefinite delivery contracts that a firm has as well. Also, assess the available capacity of key disciplines to perform the work in the required time. E. Location in the general geographic area of the project and knowledge of the locality: This factor evaluates the response time from the ES firms design office from the location of work to the Erie VA Medical Center. The personnel identified as the design team staff are expected to work in the design office identified for evaluation of this factor. NOTE: Time will be measured from the Erie VA Medical Center, Erie, PA via car to the firms indicated office where

description: Amendment 0002 dated 28 August 2026, is posted with attachments to provide the Government's answer to some questions received and DRAFT DD254; see amendment block 14 for other details. title: NOI to Sole Source for Visor Strap Assembly for T-6 Helmet
description: The integration of the dual-visor system in the T-6 aircraft will significantly enhance aircrew safety and operational efficiency by eliminating the hazardous requirement to physically swap visors during flight. By allowing pilots to seamlessly transition between clear and tinted visors, this upgrade mitigates the risk of introducing Foreign Object Debris (FOD) into the cockpit and drastically reduces "head-down" time and distraction during critical, high-workload phases of flight. Ultimately, this modernization ensures continuous eye protection against glare, bird strikes, or canopy fragmentation while maintaining optimal situational awareness, thereby directly lowering the mishap potential within the T-6 training environment.

The works will include maintaining the office accommodation, welfare facilities, kitchens, toilets, communal areas and associated spaces to a consistently high standard of cleanliness and hygiene, in accordance with the project requirements, agreed cleaning schedules and all relevant health and safety legislation. The subcontractor will be responsible for providing suitably trained and competent personnel, together with appropriate supervision, to ensure the services are delivered safely, efficiently and to the required standard. All cleaning products, materials and equipment must be suitable for their intended use and compliant with relevant COSHH requirements. All operatives undertaking the works must hold a valid CSCS card and Highways Passports. The Lower Thames Crossing is a new road that will improve connections between Essex and Kent through a tunnel beneath the River Thames. Our purpose is to drive change in how infrastructure is delivered-connecting people to jobs and businesses to opportunities, while leaving a lasting skills legacy for local communities and championing biodiversity and low-carbon construction. To support the project's ambitions, we are committed to publishing opportunities on Contracts Finder to provide full visibility to SMEs and local subcontractors. This widens access to the Lower Thames Crossing supply chain, encourages participation from smaller and locally based businesses, supports regional growth and ensures that organisations of all sizes have a fair opportunity to compete. Our ambition is to deliver the UK's greenest road while doing the right thing for local communities and the environment. Achieving this will require the support of our supply chain. Any supplier seeking to secure work on the Lower Thames Crossing must therefore demonstrate its commitment to supporting the following project ambitions: Leaving a skills legacy for the local community by recruiting locally and upskilling the workforce to enable meaningful progression into higher-paid and higher-skilled employment. Delivering the Lower Thames Crossing with the lowest practicable carbon, including supporting our zero-emissions ambitions, reducing the use of diesel on site and promoting alternative sustainable fuels and working practices. Creating opportunities through early-career roles, including apprenticeships, and inspiring young people to consider careers in construction through STEM engagement. Additional information: Please complete the attached expression of interest form and return to eleanor.clarke@skanska.co.uk

title: SOLE SOURCE: Snow Removal Services for the NWS WFO located in Caribou, Maine.
description: The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration�s (NOAA) Acquisition and Grants Office, Eastern Acquisition Division-Kansas City intends to negotiate and award a purchase order with Base plus four Option Years, on a sole source basis, under authority of RFO FAR 6.103-1, with the Town of Houlton for Snow Removal Services for the NWS WFO located in Caribou, Maine. Sole Source Justification: The Government intends to award a purchase order with base plus four option years to the Town of Houlton for the procurement of snow removal services due to their exclusive rights to the property in which the NWS WFO is located. The Town of Houlton owns and operates the Houlton International Airport where the FAA ASOS equipment is located. The Town Manager and the Public Works Director, have determined that all public works tasks at the airport shall be provided only by town public works employees. No other vendors or contractors are allowed on the airport site. Failure to have snow removal performed around and leading to the ASOS would prevent NWS technicians from performing required preventive and corrective maintenance during the snow season. A lack of observations would severely hinder, if not hinder completely, the government's ability to provide accurate terminal forecasts for safety of flight at the airport during adverse weather conditions. This pre-solicitation notice is not a request for competitive proposals and no solicitation package is available. However, firms that believe they can fully meet the government�s requirements may submit substantiating documentation or a request for additional information in writing to the (Contract Specialist) within 15 days after publication of this presolicitation notice. Such requests and documentation will be evaluated solely for the purpose of determining whether or not to conduct this procurement on a competitive basis. A determination by the government not to conduct a competitive procurement, based upon responses to this notice, is solely within the discretion of the government. Oral communications are not acceptable in response to this pre-solicitation notice.

title: Draft SOW and PSpec for Extendable Boom Forklift (EBFL)
description: Amendment 01: The purpose of this amendment is to update the deadline for submitting industry questions and feedback regarding the Draft Statement of Work (SOW) and Performance Specification (PSpec) for the Extendable Boom Forklift (EBFL). The deadline for submitting the Q&A Matrix Template has been changed to September 03, 2026 at 12:00 PM EDT. __________________________ This posting announces the release of Draft Statement of Work (SOW) and Performance Specification (PSpec) for the Extendable Boom Forklift (EBFL), see attached. The primary objective of this notice is to provide industry partners with a comprehensive understanding of the mission requirements and submit technical clarification questions before the Government finalizes its formal Request for Proposals (RFP). It is important to clarify that the government is not currently soliciting or negotiating formal proposals through this draft. The focus of this phase is strictly on refining the acquisition's technical and administrative requirements to ensure clarity and feasibility. This draft SOW and PSpec remains non-binding, and all infoDraftrmation contained within is subject to further modification based on continued evaluation and industry input. The EBFL is a diesel-powered, rough-terrain telehandler engineered to transport, load, and unload tactical cargo weighing up to 11,000 pounds. A primary focus of this draft is the forklift's ability to operate reliably over uneven and severe terrain, including sand, snow, and mud, while handling sensitive payloads such as ammunition, general cargo, and expeditionary supplies. The draft specifications outline strict lifting and dimensional thresholds that the replacement vehicle must achieve. The system must support a rated capacity of 11,000 pounds at a 24-inch load center, or 7,000 pounds at a 48-inch load center, utilizing two separate quick-attach, detachable carriages capable of adjusting fork tine widths from 0 to 76 inches. Additionally, the draft mandates the capability to handle fully loaded 463L pallets (88x108 inches) weighing up to 10,000 pounds at a 54-inch load center. For standard logistics, the forklift must be capable of loading and unloading a 4,000-pound standard military pallet (40x48 inches) into an 8x8x20-foot ISO container elevated on a Marine Corps tactical vehicle or trailer, while maintaining physical compatibility with transport assets like CH-53E/K aircraft. All industry questions and feedback regarding these draft documents must be submitted utilizing the attached Q&A Matrix Templated (Attachment 1). Incomplete rows will not receive a Government response. Email Subject Line: EBFL Draft SOW/PSpec Questions -[Contractor Name]. All emails must adhere to the above format. Responses must be emailed to Stefanie Conway at stefanie.conway@usmc.mil no later than 03 Sept 2026@ 12pm EDT.

title: BONNET CARRE SPILLWAY ROTARY CUTTER SUPPLY CONTRACT St. Charles Parish, LA
description: The contractor shall provide Rotary Cutter mowing Units for Bonnet Carre Spillway as outlined in the Bidding Schedule and Material & Requirements Paragraphs. The contractor is responsible for purchasing and delivery of the units to the Bonnet Carre Spillway's project maintenance yard (16302 River Rd., Norco, LA). Furnish the number of tractor towed Rotary Cutters (Mowers) indicated in the bid schedule. Mowers shall have 15 foot total cutting width with two flexible wings. title: Draft SOW and PSpec for Extendable Boom Forklift (EBFL)
description: This posting announces the release of Draft Statement of Work (SOW) and Performance Specification (PSpec) for the Extendable Boom Forklift (EBFL), see attached. The primary objective of this notice is to provide industry partners with a comprehensive understanding of the mission requirements and submit technical clarification questions before the Government finalizes its formal Request for Proposals (RFP). It is important to clarify that the government is not currently soliciting or negotiating formal proposals through this draft. The focus of this phase is strictly on refining the acquisition's technical and administrative requirements to ensure clarity and feasibility. This draft SOW and PSpec remains non-binding, and all infoDraftrmation contained within is subject to further modification based on continued evaluation and industry input. The EBFL is a diesel-powered, rough-terrain telehandler engineered to transport, load, and unload tactical cargo weighing up to 11,000 pounds. A primary focus of this draft is the forklift's ability to operate reliably over uneven and severe terrain, including sand, snow, and mud, while handling sensitive payloads such as ammunition, general cargo, and expeditionary supplies. The draft specifications outline strict lifting and dimensional thresholds that the replacement vehicle must achieve. The system must support a rated capacity of 11,000 pounds at a 24-inch load center, or 7,000 pounds at a 48-inch load center, utilizing two separate quick-attach, detachable carriages capable of adjusting fork tine widths from 0 to 76 inches. Additionally, the draft mandates the capability to handle fully loaded 463L pallets (88x108 inches) weighing up to 10,000 pounds at a 54-inch load center. For standard logistics, the forklift must be capable of loading and unloading a 4,000-pound standard military pallet (40x48 inches) into an 8x8x20-foot ISO container elevated on a Marine Corps tactical vehicle or trailer, while maintaining physical compatibility with transport assets like CH-53E/K aircraft. All industry questions and feedback regarding these draft documents must be submitted utilizing the attached Q&A Matrix Templated (Attachment 1). Incomplete rows will not receive a Government response. Email Subject Line: EBFL Draft SOW/PSpec Questions -[Contractor Name]. All emails must adhere to the above format. Responses must be emailed to Stefanie Conway at stefanie.conway@usmc.mil no later than 27 August 2026@ 12pm EDT.

title: NX EQ Hemodiafiltration Units
description: This Notice of Intent to Sole Source is not a request for competitive quotations or proposals. The Department of Veterans Affairs intends to negotiate and award a firm-fixed-price sole-source Requirements contract, in accordance with FAR 6.103-1(b), to a Large Business for the brand name Fresenius 5008XTM CAREsystem Hemodiafiltration Units and associated accessories. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 334510, Electromedical and Electrotherapeutic Apparatus Manufacturing, with a small business size standard of 1,250 employees. The Product Service Code (PSC) is 6515, Medical and Surgical Instruments, Equipment, and Supplies. The statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition is 41 U.S.C. � 3304(a)(1), as implemented by FAR 6.103-1(b), �Authorized or required by statute.�. Interested parties may identify their interest and capability to meet this requirement. Any response must include sufficient detail to demonstrate the ability to provide all line items described below. No solicitation is available, and telephone requests will not be accepted. Responses received will be considered; however, the Government�s decision whether to compete this requirement based on responses to this notice remains solely within the Government�s discretion. The Government will not reimburse any costs incurred by contractors in responding to this notice, nor for the Government�s use of any information received. Requirement Description Hemodiafiltration Units are extracorporeal blood purification units used in renal replacement therapy and designed to combine diffusion and convection to remove uremic toxins, excess electrolytes, and fluid from blood. The unit operates by withdrawing blood from the patient through a vascular access line and circulating it through a dialyzer containing a semi-permeable membrane; small solutes diffuse across the membrane into a countercurrent flow of dialysate, while larger molecular weight substances are removed via convective transport driven by transmembrane pressure, with a controlled volume of plasma water filtered and replaced by sterile substitution fluid. Core components include a blood pump that regulates extracorporeal blood flow, a dialyzer (filter cartridge) that facilitates solute exchange and ultrafiltration, a dialysate delivery system that prepares and circulates electrolyte-balanced fluid, a substitution fluid system that infuses replacement fluid either pre- or post-filter, pressure monitors and sensors, air detectors and venous clamps, anticoagulation systems to prevent clotting within the circuit, and a central control unit with software that coordinates flow rates, pressures, fluid balance, and treatment parameters.

title: Electronic Key Box System
description: This service is for the procurement, installation, configuration, and commissioning of a modern electronic smart key box system to support secure, auditable management of physical brass keys used by the Security Services Office (SSO), the Security Operations Center (SOC), and other authorized CDC personnel. Many CDC facilities utilize brass keys either as the primary means of access (for non?PACS?controlled spaces) or as a redundant fallback method when PACS doors are unavailable due to power, controller, network, or hardware failure. Improving the 3 accountability and security of these keys is critical to protecting CDC assets, staff, and facilities. The purpose of this requirement is to strengthen the physical security posture of CDC facilities by deploying an enterprise class smart key management platform that: � Improves accountability and traceability of key issuance and return. � Reduces risk associated with loss, misuse, or unauthorized access to controlled keys. � Provides SOC with real?time visibility into key access events. � Supports PIV credentials and MFA methods, including PIN and/or biometrics. � Integrates seamlessly with CDC networks, SOC consoles, and SSO workflows. � Ensures operational continuity through backup power and controlled manual override capabilities. � Supports overall OSSAM/SSO mission readiness in alignment with CDC security policies. These systems will be installed and integrated at the following locations: � Roybal Campus, Building 20 (SOC) � 80-key capacity. � Roybal Campus, Building 17 � 40-key capacity. � Roybal Campus, Building 18 � 40-key capacity. � Roybal Campus, Building 23 � 40-key capacity. � Chamblee Campus, Building 106 � 40-key capacity. � Lawrenceville Campus � 20-key capacity.This project will modernize the outdated systems and processes CDC�s asset key control. The SOC manages access to all high value and restricted spaces mostly but also to regular calls for service of lockouts. The current key box is outdate and often fails through long down periods. Specialist are using manual and outdated procedures to issue key defeating the original intent of an electronic key control box. The number and placement of the boxes also reduces the risk of losing a key as well as traversing campuses across the metro Atlanta area.

title: RFB to Lease the Joshua Brooks House
description: Summary of the Opportunity This Request for Bids (RFB) provides the opportunity for interested individuals and organizations to submit bids to the National Park Service (NPS) to lease NPS property for residential use (single family) at Minute Man National Historical Park under the following general terms and conditions. See attached �Draft Lease� for complete terms of occupancy. Property Offered for Lease Joshua Brooks House The Joshua Brooks House is located at 41 North Great Road, Lincoln, MA 01773. It is approximately 2,216 SF with 3 bedrooms and 2 bathrooms. It was built by Deacon Joshua Brooks circa 1780 and is situated on an approximately 0.75-acre site. The Joshua Brooks House has been completely renovated with an attached carriage house which could be used for a small car or bikes and kayaks. The first floor is spacious with a redesigned kitchen including new stainless-steel appliances, cabinetry and quartzite counter tops. The newly refinished floors reflect the natural light from meticulously restored windows. The first-floor full bathroom was recently renovated, and a new smart washer and dryer have been installed in the nearby mudroom. Two stairways lead to the second floor where there is a dedicated office, 3 bedrooms, and another recently renovated full bathroom. The house features a restored terraced seating patio overlooking Elm Brook and surrounding forest and active agricultural fields. Uses of the Leased Property This lease is most suitable for low-impact, non-transient, residential occupancy of the house. The lessee is authorized to use the property as an occupant of the house and must be willing to become a part of the National Historical Park�s relationship with the public by maintaining the historic and well-tended appearance of the structure and grounds. In accordance with the attached draft lease, the lessee is responsible for all utilities and routine maintenance. The lessor will perform basic maintenance of the property as described in the lease. Term of Lease The lease will have a maximum term of three years, and a minimum term of one year. Lessee termination rights (termination without cause) will begin 90 days before the end of the first year of the lease and continue until the lease expires. Please note: 90 days� notice is required for termination without cause. Fair Market Value Rent The lessee will be required by the lease to pay at least fair market value rent to the NPS. Based on the terms included in the attached Lease (Section 5. Rent), the minimum fair market value rent has been determined to be $59,100 annually, payable in equal monthly installments of $4,925 each month. The lessee shall pay to the United States as rent the sum of Fifty-nine Thousand, One-Hundred Dollars ($59,100.00) per year as the base rent payable to the National Park Service and forwarded by the lessee to the Superintendent, Minute Man National Historical Park. Rent checks will be mailed to Minute Man National Historical Park, 174 Liberty Street Concord, MA 01742, attention Superintendent. The annual rent shall be paid on the 1st day of each month in advance monthly installments of Four-Thousand Nine-Hundred and Twenty-five Dollars ($4,925.00). Payment covering the first month will be submitted with the executed lease. Other Terms and Conditions None. Competitive Process This lease opportunity is open to all interested persons on a competitive basis. The bidder submitting a responsive bid offering the highest monthly rent will be selected for award of the lease (subject to a determination of financial capability and reference check). A responsive bid is a bid that meets the material terms and conditions of this request for bids (see attached lease terms). The bid must offer a rental amount that is no less than fair market value as stated above. If two or more bids are equal, a drawing shall make the lease award by lot limited to the equal responsive bids received. Initial and Rolling Bid Submissions Bids must be received by the date listed on the first page of this RFB and must be submitted electronically in the format provided on the following pages. A public bid opening will occur the next day after the Initial Bid Submission Deadline (or the following Monday if the deadline is on a Friday). If a winning bid is not selected on that date, the NPS will open bids every following Monday at 1:00 PM until a responsive bid has been submitted or until NPS terminates the solicitation. Authority This RFB is issued under the authority of federal law and regulations. The applicable law is found in United States Code at 54 USC 1021 and leasing regulations may be found in the Code of Federal Regulations at 36 CFR Part 18. This RFB and the offered lease are subject to and incorporate all terms and conditions of Part 18 as applicable. In the event of any conflict between the terms of this RFB and Part 18, Part 18 controls. For Further Information Please Contact: Mike McCarthy Administrative Officer Minute Man National Historical Park 174 Liberty Street Concord, MA 01742 Phone: (781) 472-0970 E-mail: mike_mccarthy@nps.gov NPS reserves the right at any time and in NPS� sole discretion, to cause or do any or all of the following: Waive or correct any defect or technical error as to form or content of this RFB or in any bid, response, proposal, or proposal procedure, as part of the RFB or any subsequent selection and negotiation process. Modify, amend, cancel, or suspend any and all aspects of the RFB and selection process. Reissue an RFB. Modify the scope of the Lease or the required responses or modify the components of the Lease. Request that Respondents clarify, supplement, or modify the information submitted. Extend deadlines for accepting RFB responses, or request amendments to responses after expiration of deadlines. Consider comparable projects owned, developed, or operated by a Respondent. To learn more about the National Park Service, visit our website at www.nps.gov. This site includes information about who we are, our mission, NPS policies and individual parks. title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source - Victoria University
description: This is a notice of intent to award a sole source contract in accordance with Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulations Overhaul (RFO) 12.102(a). Contracting Officers may solicit from one source if it's determined only one source is reasonably available to satisfy agency requirements, as supplemented with additional information in this notice. The U.S. Department of Commerce (DOC), Office of Acquisition Management (OAM), Shared Services Procurement Office (SSPO), located in Washington, D.C., intends to negotiate on a sole-source basis and award a contract to Centre of Policy Studies (CoPS), Victoria University on behalf of the International Trade Administration (ITA. This acquisition is being conducted under the authority of permitting restricting competition in accordance with the Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul (RFO) 12.102(a) and in accordance with 41 U.S.C. 1901. This acquisition will result in a purchase order for a 12-month period The Government requires the Centre of Policy Studies (CoPS), Victoria University, to develop and deliver five integrated economic-modeling projects and associated technical materials during a 12-month period of performance. The work will provide model enhancements, updated baseline data, disaggregation capabilities, documentation, simulation files, illustrative applications, and training materials that Department staff can incorporate into internal analytical workflows. ITA requires highly specialized CGE model-development services that build directly upon modeling systems and extensions developed and maintained by CoPS. For more than 10 years, Department of Commerce offices have worked with CoPS to develop dynamic CGE models of the U.S. and global economies. The Department has used these models for trade policy, industrial policy, supply-chain, and macroeconomic analyses, including high-priority Section 232 economic analyses. CoPS possesses specialized expertise in the GTAP, GTAP-Fin, USAGE, and USAGE-TERM modeling frameworks that form the technical foundation of this requirement. The proposed work is not a stand-alone generic modeling effort; it requires modification and extension of existing CoPS-developed model structures, databases, calibration methods, disaggregation techniques, and analytical tools already used by Department economists. CoPS also has demonstrated experience developing SGMC extensions, handling detailed trade-data concordances, building dynamic CGE models, and producing the documentation and training needed for Department analysts to use those model enhancements. The requirement depends on continuity with the Department�s existing CoPS-developed models and on specialized knowledge of their underlying architecture. The five projects are designed to modify or extend those existing systems: incorporating pure profits and SGMC into trade-policy analysis; modeling sluggish tariff pass-through; updating GTAP-Fin U.S. trade data; creating a reusable GTAP-Fin disaggregation facility; and extending USAGE/USAGE-TERM to identify trade by source and destination with flexible aggregation. Based on the technical requirement described in the PWS and CoPS proposal, another source would need to recreate or independently master these existing model structures before performing the required enhancements, creating substantial duplication of effort and technical risk. Accordingly, CoPS is uniquely positioned to perform the required work while maintaining compatibility with the Department�s existing analytical capabilities. As previously stated, this is NOT a solicitation for quotations, quotation abstracts, a request for competitive quotations; or request for competitive proposals; There is no solicitation package available for review due to the Government�s intention to conduct this requirement as a sole source award. If a company determines that their company can meet all requirements mentioned above, the company shall submit a written response within 15 days from the date of publication of this synopsis for it to be taken into consideration by the Government. Responses must clearly and thoroughly defend any claims or assertions that attempt to refute the Government�s claim. A determination by the Government not to proceed with this proposed action based upon responses to this notice is solely with the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. Information received on this notice must eliminate the Government's concerns and address how the required services can be provided. If no qualified/affirmative responses are received within 15 days of this notice to determine whether a qualified source is more advantageous to the Government, a contract will be awarded to Centre of Policy Studies (CoPS), Victoria University.
